item.title: Angie Martinez Explains Why Tupac's Unheard Interview Stayed Locked Away
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Angie Martinez brings her guarded Tupac recording to Netflix with guests who revisit the history behind the conversation.
item.content:encoded:
Angie Martinez is ready to share Tupac’s unreleased interview without letting its most heated moments tell the whole story.

Her four-part Netflix project revisits a conversation she kept largely private for three decades.

Martinez told Netflix’s Tudum that releasing everything in 1996 could have damaged relationships and intensified an already dangerous conflict.

Tupac’s death made the decision harder because she didn’t want the recording treated as his final statement.

Martinez explained why she reconsidered keeping the recording private: “I also realized these tapes were bigger than me.”

The series brings in Charlamagne Tha God, Joe Budden, Big Boy, Dream Hampton, RZA and Wallo.

Martinez told Tudum, “The difference now is that I have the opportunity to share them with context.”

She wants the discussion to examine the circumstances around the recording rather than simply circulate its most provocative passages.

That concern has followed the tapes for years, long before Netflix entered the picture.

In a 2017 discussion about releasing the interview, Martinez said she’d tried to contact Tupac’s mother to ask how she wanted it handled.

Afeni Shakur’s death interrupted that effort, leaving Martinez without a settled release plan.

She still intended to make the recording public eventually, but respecting the people connected to it remained part of the decision.

The interview had already become part of Martinez’s own career story through her 2016 memoir, My Voice.

That book also revisited her move from Hot 97 to Power 105.1 and the artist disputes she’d navigated along the way.

Those pages covered more than the stories that made it onto her broadcasts. Martinez also revisited her role mediating artists’ disputes and the decisions that came with interviewing some of rap’s biggest names.

J. Cole supplied the book’s foreword as Martinez put those experiences on the page.

The memoir became a New York Times bestseller, bringing her radio career and recollections to another audience.

By the time of her 2017 Reddit appearance, the unreleased conversation was described as a two-hour recording. Martinez acknowledged the demand to hear it while declining to give a timetable she hadn’t worked out.

The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez arrives on Netflix November 27.

item.title: Snoop Dogg Books Jamie Foxx & Martha Stewart For NBC Christmas Special
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Snoop Dogg lines up a star-packed NBC holiday hangout as Death Row Pictures keeps building its television and film business.
item.content:encoded:
Snoop Dogg is turning an NBC hotel-suite party into another television job for himself and a holiday invitation for Jamie Foxx. Martha Stewart’s coming too, joining a guest list that stretches from his music circle to comedy and Broadway.

“Christmas With Snoop” airs December 2 at 10 p.m. on NBC, with Peacock carrying the special the following day, according to Variety.

The setup brings that celebration to television with friends and loved ones gathered in a plush suite for the festivities.

Jane Handcock and October London are among those booked for appearances and musical performances, alongside Foxx and his daughter Anelise. Wayne Brady, Kristin Chenoweth, Adam Devine, Craig Robinson, Nicole Scherzinger and Gwen Stefani also join the lineup.

Snoop’s got a role behind the camera as well, executive producing alongside Sara Ramaker through Death Row Pictures. Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay are executive producers for Jesse Collins Entertainment, bringing another production company into the holiday gathering.

That producer credit connects the special to a bigger piece of Snoop’s business.

His Death Row Pictures signed a multiyear creative partnership with NBCUniversal in 2025 covering film, television, sports entertainment and streaming, giving the relationship room beyond guest appearances.

The company already has his life story headed for theaters, with Jonathan Daviss playing him and Craig Brewer directing.

AllHipHop recently reported that Hercy Miller will portray his father Master P in the movie, which also casts Cynthia Erivo as Afeni Shakur.

The Christmas booking also builds on Snoop’s work across NBC’s biggest entertainment and sports broadcasts. He’s coached on “The Voice” and contributed to Olympic coverage, including Paris in 2024 and Milan-Cortina earlier this year.

His Paris Olympics work earned two Sports Emmys as part of NBCUniversal’s coverage, including the award for Outstanding Live Special – Championship Event.

Those assignments have put the Long Beach rapper in front of audiences far beyond his recording career.

This time, the network’s handing him a holiday special with familiar collaborators while his production company takes a place in the credits.

Universal Pictures has set the Snoop biopic’s upcoming theatrical release for August 6, 2027.

item.title: Rod Wave Defends Jay-Z’s Age: “That’s The Goal”
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Rod Wave explains why Jay-Z's longevity carries weight for him as he studies older artists and grows his own businesses.
item.content:encoded:
Rod Wave sees Jay-Z’s age as something to aspire to because staying alive and successful was never guaranteed where he grew up.

The rapper explained his respect for older artists during a conversation with Ari Melber.

Instead of measuring Jay-Z against younger rappers, Rod described watching his decisions for lessons he can apply to his own future.

“So now that I get out here in the world, I have to look at guys like Jay who succeeded, and people might say he’s old or whatever the case may be, but in my eyes, just guys don’t get to be that old where I’m from or the hand that we was dealt, guys don’t get to be that successful,” Rod Wave said.

He connected that outlook to the people who shaped him before music became his livelihood.

Their influence mattered, he explained, but navigating his current life also required studying people who had already reached places he wanted to go.

“So I have to look at guys like that and just take what I can take from it and in some kind of way, because that’s the goal, to make it to that age and still be successful, still be talked about, still have opinions and, and stuff like that,” Rod Wave said.

Jay-Z was part of a broader approach to learning from established artists.

“It’s the same thing with Drake. It’s the same thing with Kanye. It’s the same thing with all these guys who are before me,” Rod Wave said.

Rod described weighing which choices to follow and which to avoid. His admiration did not mean copying every decision; he was looking for useful experience from artists further along in their careers.

That interest in building something lasting comes as his own business expands beyond records.

AllHipHop previously reported on Mainstay Sports’ growing roster, while the Mainstay umbrella also includes touring and film operations.

Mainstay Touring produced his Don’t Look Down Tour, and Mainstay Films handled its trailer. The sports agency launched in August.

Arkansas freshman Abdou Toure joined Mainstay Sports in October for marketing and brand representation.

item.title: WhoKnowCorey Shares His Mindset on Growth and Opportunity With “Put You On”
item.dc:creator: Brxton Lee
item.description: WhoKnowCorey blends Southern roots with ambition and loyalty on “Put You On,” a single about creating opportunities and bringing others along as he grows.
item.content:encoded:
WhoKnowCorey, an emerging artist, is leveraging his latest single “Put You On” to educate fans on the attitude that guides his music. The song is based on concepts of ambition, loyalty, and the significance of opportunities, as the artist becomes more comfortable with himself while considering the implications of success on those surrounding him.

The phrase “put you on” means much more to WhoKnowCorey than just introducing someone  to a song, contact, or experience. Instead, it refers to the possibility to make other people move further by educating them, providing opportunities, and offering them a unique perspective. This forms the basis for his single and adds a personal touch.

“I want listeners to get the message that success does not have to be a one-person game,” he says. “When you find something good, whether it’s an opportunity, a connection, or a new perspective, don’t be afraid to share it with others.”

WhoKnowCorey Looks at Success Beyond Himself

The message behind “Put You On” is drawn from experiences, relationships, and lessons that have influenced WhoKnowCorey’s development. Rather than presenting achievement as something that happens in isolation, he approaches the subject through the idea that people can help one another reach new levels. In some cases, a simple conversation, a connection, or simply sharing some information may alter someone’s path.

This perspective also affects the way the artist views his own status as an up and coming performer. His single conveys the ambitions he has and the progress he is striving to achieve but also highlights the benefits that he plans to offer his supporters. He wants listeners to understand his goals without losing sight of the people and experiences that have contributed to his journey.

“To me, ‘Put You On’ means putting people in a position to win, introducing them to new opportunities, and helping them see a different side of life.”

Background in Louisiana and Texas Influences His Music

WhoKnowCorey’s musical identity draws from his Louisiana and Texas background, combining Southern energy, catchy melodies, and personal storytelling. He credits Louisiana with contributing a distinctive flavor and soul to his sound, while Texas has influenced his flow, confidence, and overall approach.

The influences allow him to relate to his roots but give him a chance to follow his own path. Instead of trying to copy someone else’s style, he is working on his own. Music has been part of his life since he was 15, giving him years to learn, experiment, and gradually establish his own approach. He sees the new single as evidence of that development, particularly in the way he is learning to communicate his perspective through his records.

“‘Put You On’ represents a new chapter for me, showing people who I am as an artist and what I’m capable of becoming,” WhoKnowCorey mentions.

Building on the Release

Now that “Put You On” is out, WhoKnowCorey will be looking to keep up a steady release schedule, try out new things with his music, and connect more closely with his fans. He is also excited about the possibility of collaborating with musicians that have different approaches to their art.

Looking ahead, some of his long-term goals involve creating a sustainable career, finding a strong fanbase, and playing bigger gigs, all while bringing more attention to his Louisiana and Texas background. This gives the song context as part of a larger path, rather than being an isolated release.

For anyone discovering WhoKnowCorey’s work through “Put You On,” the song presents a chance to learn about an artist who wants to blend Southern musical traditions with his own perspective on success, loyalty, and perseverance. While he continues to refine his sound and direction, he sees this release as a way of letting his audience know what motivates him and where he is headed.

item.title: Yella Beezy Passed Out, Collapsed After MO3 Murder Verdict
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Yella Beezy reportedly collapsed after his MO3 murder conviction, while claims that shock caused the incident remain unconfirmed.
item.content:encoded:
You definitely could see the shock in his eyes if you look closely. He asked to kiss his son before he went away.

Yella Beezy reportedly collapsed behind the courtroom after receiving a verdict that will send him to prison for life. He held it together while he was in the courtroom. His face looked stunned. Shortly thereafter, he allegedly passed out. We don’t have any medical verdict on this, but it certainly looks like it was related to the verdict against him. And that verdict was something that stunned a lot of people.

The Dallas rapper’s case took another distressing turn Wednesday after jurors found him guilty of capital murder in MO3’s killing. NBC 5 reported that it was told Conway “fell out in the back hall” once he was officially taken into custody. No account confirms fully that he actually lost consciousness. 

Now, descriptions of Beezy being overwhelmed by disbelief need a little breathing room. We do not access to his thoughts. The internet has enough honorary doctors without us handing out another diploma. Nevertheless, he went to trial so we can we can assess it from there. If you go to trial in cases like this, you probably believe you’re going to beat it.

Dallas County officials announced that Beezy, whose legal name is Markies Conway, was convicted November 11 and sentenced to life without the possibility of parole. The verdict arrived exactly six years after MO3, born Melvin Noble, was killed on a Dallas interstate. Prosecutors established that Conway arranged and financed the killing, according to the district attorney’s office. 

Inside the courtroom, the aftermath was emotional. NBC 5 reported that Beezy asked to kiss his young son, who also left the room crying. The station witnessed several people in tears. Whatever readers think of the verdict, a child experiencing that moment deserves compassion. Damn.

Beezy pleaded not guilty, and his defense is preparing to challenge the outcome. Attorney Toby Shook expressed disappointment and said the team intends to keep fighting through an appeal. 

That leaves us with a serious distinction to maintain as this story travels through Hip-Hop: the conviction is established, the hallway incident is attributed reporting, and the explanation for that incident remains unconfirmed.

There is plenty to examine without turning somebody’s possible medical episode into a punchline.

MO3’s family has endured six years of loss. Beezy’s family is confronting a life sentence. An appeal may bring further arguments, but neither family gets to simply close the browser and move on.

at the same time, we should get serious about unpacking, but all of this really means. Because it is a lot. And a lot of people have things to say that are off base, on base and really, truly shockingly real.

item.title: Lil Kim Gets “Hard Core” Empire State Building Tribute For 30th Anniversary
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lil Kim's Hard Core turns 30 with an Empire State Building tribute and two orchestral hometown shows at Kings Theatre.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Kim will have the Empire State Building glowing pink for the 30th anniversary of Hard Core, the album that launched her solo career.

The building’s official lighting calendar confirms the tribute for Thursday, November 12, under the listing “In Celebration of the 30th Anniversary of Lil’ Kim’s Debut Album HARD CORE.”

That skyline salute comes just before Kim takes the anniversary celebration back to Brooklyn for two nights at Kings Theatre.

Her Hard Core Symphony concerts are scheduled for November 18 and 19, with Thee Phantom & The Illharmonic Orchestra joining her onstage.

The dates expand the plans AllHipHop covered when Kim first announced the orchestral concert in August.

That announcement offered one November 19 performance, while the venue’s current schedule gives fans a second chance to catch the show a night earlier.

The music will come from an all-Black ensemble that brings Hip-Hop and R&B together with live orchestral arrangements.

Concert plans call for songs including “Big Momma Thang,” “Crush On You,” “No Time” and the “Not Tonight” remix, alongside material from her wider catalog.

The musicians have performed at Carnegie Hall, the Kennedy Center and the Apollo Theater during more than 25 years together.

Hard Core arrived in 1996 with The Notorious B.I.G. serving as executive producer, and the album earned double-platinum certification.

Kim kept that commercial run going with two more platinum albums, The Notorious K.I.M. in 2000 and La Bella Mafia in 2003. Her early singles run also delivered three consecutive No. 1 hits on Billboard’s rap chart.

The Empire State Building connection also reaches back to the rapper who helped introduce her to a national audience.

In 2022, AllHipHop reported plans for a Biggie 50th-birthday salute featuring red and white lights with a crown display. Kim was among the guests announced for that ceremony alongside Lil Cease and members of Biggie’s family.

For her own anniversary shows, fans will hear those records in a black-tie setting rather than a standard concert presentation. Kings Theatre requires formal attire for the performances at 1027 Flatbush Avenue, with both shows starting at 8 p.m.

Doors open at 7 p.m. for both of the Brooklyn concerts.

item.title: Tim Westwood Denies Two More Charges As January Trial Nears
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Tim Westwood fights the latest allegations in a 17-count case as his London court proceedings move toward a January trial.
item.content:encoded:
Tim Westwood has entered fresh not-guilty pleas in London to contest two additional sexual-offense charges before his criminal case reaches trial in January. The former Hip-Hop radio host now denies all 17 counts involving nine women.

Thursday’s hearing at Southwark Crown Court addressed allegations from 1991 and 2004, according to Sky News. Westwood, 69, pleaded not guilty to both during the brief court appearance.

Prosecutors added those counts in September, so Thursday brought his formal response rather than another expansion of the case. AllHipHop previously covered the two additional charges when authorities announced them.

One count concerns an alleged indecent assault in Hammersmith and Fulham involving a girl who was 16 or 17. The other alleges a sexual assault against an 18-year-old woman in Wandsworth in May 2004.

The Crown Prosecution Service identified the first alleged incident as occurring in January 1991. Its September announcement also specified that the newer allegations involve two women beyond the seven included in the original prosecution.

Westwood had already indicated that he would contest the additional charges when he appeared at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on October 23. That appearance ended with conditional bail until Thursday’s hearing.

The earlier case includes two sexual-assault counts, four rape counts and nine indecent-assault counts. Those charges were brought in October 2025, and Westwood subsequently entered not-guilty pleas to each of them. The original allegations include three indecent assaults said to have occurred at BBC studios in the 1990s and a Gloucestershire nightclub allegation from 2010.

Across the prosecution, the alleged offenses span 1983 through 2016. The charges remain allegations, with no verdict reached in the pending trial. “The Crown Prosecution Service reminds everyone that criminal proceedings are active, and the defendant has the right to a fair trial,” Deputy Chief Crown Prosecutor Catherine P Baccas said in September.

Westwood’s broadcasting career took him from Capital Radio to the BBC in 1994, putting him on Radio 1 and Radio 1Xtra. He later returned to commercial radio through Capital Xtra after leaving the BBC in 2013.

His Saturday program at Capital Xtra ended when he left the company in 2022.

item.title: Birdman Gets Congressional Salute For Taking New Orleans Rap National
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Birdman earns a place in the Congressional Record as Troy Carter celebrates Cash Money's New Orleans roots and national reach.
item.content:encoded:
Birdman has taken Cash Money’s New Orleans story into the Congressional Record with a tribute that puts his hometown sound first.

Rep. Troy Carter submitted remarks celebrating the label co-founder in the November 9 edition.

Carter’s written tribute follows the path from neighborhood clubs to a national record business.

It credits Birdman and his brother Slim with helping New Orleans music travel far beyond Louisiana.

The statement also remembers Kilo G’s early place on the roster and the local clubs where the brothers searched for talent.

“I am truly honored by his contributions to Bounce Music,” Carter wrote. “He has made a lasting impact on the music industry, as co-founder of Cash Money Records, a record executive, and artist, along with his brother Ronald ‘Slim’ Williams.”

The recognition sits in the record’s Extensions of Remarks section, where members can place statements honoring people and causes.

Carter makes room for the people who helped build the label, including in-house producer Mannie Fresh and the Hot Boys.

His account names Juvenile, Turk, B.G. and Lil Wayne as the group that helped Cash Money grow.

That history still has a live audience, with Cash Money and No Limit sharing a tour after building separate New Orleans empires. Birdman and Slim previously described the shows as a celebration of their city and the listeners who stayed with them.

Carter’s statement also credits the Hot Boys’ success with helping Cash Money secure its $30 million Universal deal in 1998.

The tribute treats the business expansion and the local talent behind it as parts of the same story.

The congressman’s closing salute returns to Birdman’s role in carrying New Orleans bounce outside the city.

“I am happy to celebrate [Birdman] for his amazing contributions to amplifying New Orleans Bounce Music Nationally, extending sincerest wishes that he continues to flourish in his future endeavors both in Louisiana and abroad,” Carter wrote.

The record also recognizes Birdman’s recording partnership with Mannie Fresh as the Big Tymers, whose album I Got That Work arrived in 2000.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: OTF DeDe Demands New Trial Over Missing Instagram Comments
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: OTF DeDe challenges his convictions over delayed Instagram evidence after Lil Durk beats every count in their joint trial.
item.content:encoded:
Deandre Dontrell Wilson wants a new trial over Instagram evidence his lawyer says prosecutors withheld until jurors had already watched the video. Known as OTF DeDe, the Lil Durk co-defendant argues that missing viewer comments could have helped his defense against three stalking charges.

Attorney Craig Harbaugh’s November 11 filing pushes back against prosecutors’ argument that an unsolicited email gave him access to the disputed information. Harbaugh says he didn’t read that message until November 10, long after the September verdict.

“The government had them on August 19, held on to them for seven days, and produced them only after the jury had watched the video,” Harbaugh wrote. “The government cannot outsource its duty to disclose.”

The fight concerns an Instagram Live recording and references to “Murdaman” that DeDe’s defense says needed the viewer comments for context. Harbaugh points to an agent’s interview notes listing Murdaman and DeDe separately before prosecutors played the footage on August 26.

“Regardless, a stranger’s account of a comment is not the recording the government withheld,” Harbaugh wrote. He argues that prosecutors had several opportunities to disclose the material before jurors saw their version.

Harbaugh says prosecutors acknowledged possessing the comments only after the defense objected to the video. According to his filing, prosecutor Michael Morse told the court, “we actually have the comments, but that is not the version.”

“The link reached the defense at 10:05 that night,” Harbaugh wrote. “One email at any of those four points would have ended the matter.”

DeDe became part of the investigation into the August 19, 2022 shooting targeting Quando Rondo near Los Angeles’ Beverly Center.

AllHipHop’s trial coverage detailed how investigators traced distinctive pants to Chicago stores before Chicago officers identified DeDe and supplied his Instagram account.

Account records and flight evidence then helped investigators track DeDe’s California trip alongside other alleged participants before the attack. Prosecutors described the operation as retaliation for King Von’s killing, but Quando Rondo survived while his cousin Lul Pab died.

Lil Durk beat all five charges submitted to jurors in their September 11 verdict. DeDe and Browneyez also beat both murder-for-hire counts, but jurors convicted them of conspiracy to commit stalking, stalking using a dangerous weapon and stalking resulting in death.

DeDe’s lawyer now argues that an unread message doesn’t erase prosecutors’ obligation to provide evidence favorable to the defense. “A crowded inbox does not excuse a Brady violation,” Harbaugh wrote, invoking the rule requiring prosecutors to disclose such material.

Harbaugh asks Judge Michael W. Fitzgerald to order a new trial on all three counts if the judge rejects DeDe’s separate acquittal motion.

Harbaugh’s sworn declaration says the stranger’s email contained no attachment or link and remained marked unread when he located it on November 10.

item.title: 50 Cent Offers Jensen Huang An AI Job As Nvidia CEO Resigns
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: 50 Cent offered Jensen Huang an AI job at G-Unit as Nvidia announced its founder's resignation amid an affair scandal.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent offered Jensen Huang an AI job at G-Unit as the Nvidia founder’s affair scandal reached the boardroom and ended with his resignation Thursday.

The rapper paired his pitch with an AI-generated video depicting himself and Huang, set to “P.I.M.P.” The clip is not footage of the two men together.

“Jensen don’t sweat it come be head of AI at g-unit film a television,” 50 wrote in the caption. He followed that invitation with his GreenLightGang slogan.

The joke landed amid a far more serious corporate crisis. Nvidia announced November 12 that Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately.

Finance chief Colette Kress became interim CEO while retaining her CFO duties. The board is searching inside and outside the company for a permanent replacement. It also named Harvey C. Jones its first-ever chairman.

Huang had acknowledged infidelity in a November 8 message to employees.

“I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

The scandal involves Alice Huang, a businesswoman linked to Megaspeed. She and Jensen Huang are not related. Reuters’ timeline traces the controversy to reporting about U.S. intelligence concerns over her relationship with the chip executive and suspected ties to Chinese intelligence. Those suspicions are allegations, not an established finding of espionage.

The board launched an independent investigation November 8. At that point, it said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised.

On November 10, independent directors retained former acting U.S. Attorney Joon H. Kim and Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the inquiry.

A second alleged relationship then emerged. Reuters reported that The New York Times identified Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s healthcare vice president who reported to Huang, in a November 11 report about another affair.

For 50, the pitch also plugs the company behind his Shreveport studio ambitions. His caption offers a job, but it does not announce an agreement or a hiring.
